title: A Thin Crescent, Watched From the Telescope Perch

content.question: Is the thin crescent moon really the same silver as the rest of the sky's light, or does it keep a colour of its own once the dusk has taken everything else?
content.method: At dusk, with the sky going from blue to ink, I climbed onto the telescope and sat on the high end where the lens sees furthest. I watched the crescent for a long while without blinking more than I had to, comparing its edge against the faint grey of the cloud beside it. I then looked at the dark part of the moon that the sun does not touch, which only shows as a ghost outline, and noted whether it had any tint at all.
content.result: The crescent is not white. Its lit edge leans toward a pale cream, and the unlit ghost of the disc is a cool grey-violet that the cloud does not share. I cannot prove the violet is the moon and not my own eyes, but I have written it down, and I have decided it is mine to keep.
